summary: Leaf scope holds: one behavior (tier-2 organisms become present in the production world - spawns plus their body shapes plus the single presentation spot-check ship as one testable outcome), two named changed subsystems, and at most three changed responsibilities (worldData.ts spawn entries, data-driven shape parameters on the existing WI-02b pipeline, and same-behavior checks). No new renderer architecture or simulation rule changes are in scope; defects go through the fix-planning route. Criteria AC-roster-count and AC-roster-tests are retained verbatim from WI-03b, and together with WI-03b1 the children's union covers all three parent criteria with explicit final proof owners (roster-wide count and spoiler audit in WI-03d, per parent plan). depends_on WI-03b1 is correct (spawns reference landed defs; spot-check exercises friendly rendering) and inherits the WI-02a/b/c gate via the parent path. Verification is focused: headless world-data band/resolve check, tier-scoped spoiler containment check, and one browser spot-check flagged presentation-only per section 70 layers; no arbitrary-defect-fix promise. Handoff is sufficient for a fresh session: concrete file pointer (src/world/worldData.ts), request sections 13/13.4/33/34/49/68/70/74 verified to exist in the root request, WI-01b for ids, WI-03b1 for landed ids and shape parameters, design_private/ as source of truth. Recorded assumptions: the wreck-incorporating shape is conditional on the private roster's assignment (adaptive, not hidden scope, since design_private/ is authoritative) and 'preferably a friendly one' leaves the spot-check representative choice to the implementer.
